subject.title: [Security] Missing complexity validation and rate limiting on log query filters

question: Does any client-controlled recursive filter reach SQLite through the current ACP or audit history surfaces, or should this issue be closed as unreproduced pending a concrete private proof?
rationale: Current source contradicts the alleged path, but the security label and availability claim require an authorized owner to confirm the trust boundary and disclosure route.

options.title: Confirm and close
options.body: Confirm that current ACP replay and audit RPCs expose only bounded identifier/scalar queries, then close and request a private advisory with a concrete payload if new evidence appears.

options.title: Request private reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue pending while asking the reporter to provide the exact RPC, authenticated role, payload, query plan, and measured database or CPU impact through the private security channel.

options.title: Sponsor broader hardening
options.body: Treat query-cost controls as defense-in-depth work after defining which operator-facing ledger endpoints need shared rate or execution budgets.

recommendation.title: Confirm and close
recommendation.body: Confirm that current ACP replay and audit RPCs expose only bounded identifier/scalar queries, then close and request a private advisory with a concrete payload if new evidence appears.

likelyOwner.reason: He is explicitly associated with both Agents/ACP and Security in repository ownership guidance and was mentioned on this issue.
